thread:
maria: Heads up — eu-west dedicated pool-7 showing KV cache thrash and a bunch of slowdowns. Seen after a thermal event on node gpu-7a. Latency + tail errors for multiple tenants. Anyone on-call for routing/fallback?

sam: Got the alerts, looking. Initial telemetry shows GPU mem evictions + NIC tx spikes. Could be noisy tenant or a thermal-induced perf cliff.

jess: Pasting a short snippet from the proxy logs:```
2026-02-12T09:08:22Z proxy: kvcache miss rate 0.67 -> evicting prefixes
2026-02-12T09:08:23Z runtime: gpu-7a OOM_kvcache -> slab_reclaim
2026-02-12T09:08:23Z net: tx_queue full host=gpu-7a
```

infra-bot: ALERT: node gpu-7a high_evictions (score=92) — routing_hint=DEGRADED — 1719000001

li: Can we short-circuit by evicting preemptible jobs on that host? Propose `kubectl drain gpu-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` but I know dedicated pools will break if we do blunt drains. Alternative: scheduler-level soft-eject low-priority pods.

nick: Don't drain blindly — dedicated pool has committed tenants. Short-term play: mark the host/slot as `degraded=true` in the allocator so new allocations avoid it and existing allocations can gracefully finish. We can also flip a per-pool routing override to prefer other racks.

maria: OK. I can push a quick routing override. Question: do we have a single switch to mark the whole pool as soft-isolate so allocator steers new traffic away?

sam: Yes — I can add an override: set pool-7 tag `isolation:soft` for eu-west for 10m and update the allocator weight to 0.2 for new bookings. Also will enable kvcache-proxy sticky to reduce cross-host key churn. Doing that now.

jess: Cost check: if we redirect allocations to other racks we might trigger cross-az warm-ups or spin up reserved instances. Rough estimate: additional egress and spin-up ~ $2k/hr while we rebalance. Ops budget?

maria: For this incident we can absorb short spike, but keep it tight. Please log exact egress numbers to incident.

li: Longer-term note: we should cap background batch bandwidth on noisy tenants using cgroups or NIC policing. I'll open GH issue (#1234) with proposed knobs (egress-shaper, kvcache-eviction-floor).

nick: Also rolling a tiny hotfix to routing: fallback model variant selection favoring smaller-KV footprints when `isolation=soft` so we reduce memory churn during degraded windows. That should reduce immediate pressure without evicting paid tenants.

infra-bot: ACTION: routing override applied by sam — pool-7 isolation=soft TTL=600s. Rebalancer scheduled to avoid gpu-7a for new allocs.

maria: Good. Sam, after override please watch 1m/5m p50/p99 and post numbers. Jess, keep finance informed on spend delta. Li, leave the GH issue with steps. Nick, coordinate with scheduler for graceful handoff.

sam: p50 baseline 18ms -> 25ms, p99 spikes mostly gone after override. KV miss rate dropping. Will monitor for 15m.

infra-bot: UPDATE: gpu-7a thermal profile bumped (fan +20%) by rack automation at 1719000090. Eviction rate decreasing.

maria: Nice. Once stable let's roll the host back into normal rotation slowly. Re-open if anything flares.

nick: I'll set the re-add to be staged — 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 20m to avoid re-triggering the churn.

jess: Filing incident follow-up: audit noisy preemptible tenants, add runbook steps for soft-isolate + routing override, quantify cost impact (~$1.8k estimated) and mark for Q2 infra work.

infra-bot: RESOLVED: metrics recovered. Node gpu-7a eviction score -> 12. Rebalancer will reintroduce capacity per nick's staged plan.

maria: Thanks everyone. Please add runbook entries and tag the GH issue. I'll convert this thread into a post-incident doc with TL;DR and next actions.
